after.summary: Novaya Gazeta has shut down. It was one of Russia’s best-known independent media outlets and had continued operating inside the country after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. In late October, news emerged that its journalists were being evicted from their office on Potapovsky Lane in central Moscow, where they had worked for 29 years. The publication itself had been around for 33 years. Novaya Gazeta said it was closing under pressure from the authorities and the security services. The Kremlin called the closure “a normal process of turnover,” which Novaya Gazeta’s staff left the office saying that “some media outlets cease to exist, and new ones take their place.” On November 9, the newsroom held its final editorial meeting, after which Novaya Gazeta’s staff left what was now their former office to applause.
